strongest_angle: The Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA) and the Gemini North Telescope discovered Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua (J1602+4228AB), an extraordinary pair of quasars from the Cosmic Dawn 900 million years after the Big Bang.

key_facts.fact: The Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy discovered the quasar pair Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, also designated as J1602+4228AB, located at a distance placing them 900 million years after the Big Bang.
The two monster black holes powering the quasar pair have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million times that of the sun, respectively.
The quasar pair Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is separated by a distance of approximately 18,100 light-years, which is roughly one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way galaxy.

named_entities.name: Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy
